subject: POC throughput criteria & burst matrix — next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@quanticahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: POC throughput criteria & proposed next steps

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed plan so we can get the POC scheduled: 

POC objective (agreed): validate production throughput for the patient-facing inference API while meeting latency SLAs and cost targets.

Proposed success criteria (draft):
- Sustained baseline: 250 RPS for 30m with P50 < 120ms and token cost within target range.
- Concurrency: support 150 concurrent open requests without tail-latency spikes.
- Burst handling: tolerate weekly spikes up to 5,000 RPS for 60–120s with graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model variant) and <5% error rate.
- Quality guardrail: no more than 2% deviation on label-level QA tests (we'll share eval prompts).

Workload details we need from you to finalize config:
- Typical prompt token length (avg / 95th pct), expected response token lengths.
- Typical and peak concurrency windows (time of day / frequency).
- Any client-side batching currently performed.

Attached I dropped two files: poc_success_matrix.xlsx (success criteria matrix + owner columns) and traffic-sample.json (anonymized traffic extract). Please review and flag any inaccuracies.

Tentative timeline:
- Confirm traffic spec & sign intake doc: by 2026-09-10
- Staging smoke test window: 2026-09-14 — 2026-09-18
- POC full run: 2026-09-21 — 2026-09-25

Ownership suggestions:
- Redwood infra & sizing: Ben Carter
- Success metrics & QA: Marissa Cole
- Commercial / PO coordination: Dylan (me)

Primary asks for you: confirm the traffic numbers above (token lengths, concurrency), and confirm PO timeline so we can reserve Dedicated capacity for the POC dates. Also let us know if Quantica needs a SOC2 or other security package up front — we can share the standard packet this week.

If that looks good I’ll book the staging window and send a short intake doc for signature.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: poc_success_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: traffic-sample.json (json)]

Dylan —

Thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- Typical prompt length: ~45 tokens (median), 95th pct ~110.
- Typical response length: avg ~130 tokens.
- Concurrency: baseline is ~80 concurrent open requests; we expect planned growth to ~150 over the next quarter.
- Bursts: last quarter we saw an event with a spike to ~4.8k RPS for ~90s; monthly load tests vary.

Security/PO: We will need SOC2 Type II evidence and a standard DPA before any data is routed. Procurement is asking that we get a PO ready by 9/15 so finance can release a short-term commitment.

Two asks for you: 1) can Redwood provide an estimate of expected token cost under the baseline vs. burst profile, and 2) can you confirm whether batching on the client side will be necessary/recommended given our short prompts?

Looping in platform@quanticahealth.com to track the intake.

—Emily
Emily Cho
Head of Platform Engineering | Quantica Health

Dylan / Marissa —

Saw Emily’s details. Quick ops readout and requests from infra: 
- Traffic-sample.json shows a high proportion of short prompts (median 45 tokens) and responses ~120–150 tokens. That profile favors batching on the server side; we should enable small continuous-batching windows to improve throughput without hurting latency.
- For the weekly 5k RPS 90s spike, recommend configuring burst pool with pre-warmed instances and a fallback model (quantized) to keep token cost bounded.
- Need to confirm model family (Curie-equivalent vs. Llama-family) — affects kernel selection and quantization path. Dylan: can you confirm customer preference?
- Security: POC will require SOC2 packet and a DPA; I’ll pull the SOC2 summary and share it.

Proposed split of responsibilities (to be added to the spreadsheet):
- Ben Carter: infra sizing, pre-warm policy, staging verification (smoke).
- Marissa Cole: success metrics ingestion, evaluation prompts, dashboarding for P50/P95/P99 and error rates.
- Dylan: commercial sign-off, PO coordination, customer comms.

Staging window: tentatively 2026-09-14 to 2026-09-18; schedule smoke test on 9/14 at 10:00 PT.

Action items: 
- Dylan: confirm model variant and share HubSpot PO link.
- Marissa: prepare the eval prompt set and metric templates (add to poc_success_matrix.xlsx).
- Ben: prepare SOC2 packet and quick-run pre-warm checklist.

Ben
